thesis: Local-first mobile development Nexus and production factory connecting local intelligence, frontier agents, GitHub/Memo capabilities and controlled Android execution.
confirmed_decisions: Independent from Memo; Memo is external automation connector
hypotheses: AI-assisted builders unfamiliar with Android toolchains are initial segment
Durable missions and context are differentiators
On-device builds work for a useful subset
archive_status: Original brainstorm transcript was not fully supplied; this archive combines confirmed repository decisions with a clearly labelled summary recovered from prior conversation context, not verbatim dialogue.
conversation_derived_clarifications: One natural-language development objective drives one shared durable mission engine; no keyword-selected or per-example workflows.
Local and frontier models are intelligence providers; project, GitHub, build, test, diagnostic, signing and artifact operations are separately callable scoped capabilities.
Every mission must observe actual tool output, verify postconditions, expose evidence, replan when needed and recover durable state after interruption.
Local Android project folders and GitHub repositories are equal first-class project sources using the same mission lifecycle.
Local builds must remain on-device and independent of GitHub Actions; no silent cloud fallback.
Imported projects must be snapshotted and verified before execution; build scripts are untrusted and require explicit user approval.
GitHub writes require scoped grants, immutable base revisions, reviewed diffs and explicit approvals.
Signing credentials are never available to agents; temporary CI keys must never be represented as update-safe APK signing identities.
Memo remains a separate automation connector, not a merged product.
PocketForge is a specialized native Android development factory, not an unrestricted general assistant or Android Studio clone.

branch_policy.policy: Use short-lived focused branches for active milestones; merge reviewed coherent work to main, then delete merged/stale branches. Keep only genuinely active work branches.
